story_description: Provide interactive testing and validation capabilities for hook configurations, enabling users to verify hook behavior with sample inputs before deploying to production, reducing trial-and-error debugging cycles.
task_description: Implement HookTestPanelView SwiftUI component that provides an interactive testing interface for hooks with sample input editor, example loaders, test execution, output display with timing metrics, and CLI test command generation.
atom_description: Build HookTestPanelView.swift with JSON input editor featuring syntax highlighting, three example loader buttons (Safe File, Dangerous Path, Custom), Run Test button with execution state, output panel showing formatted JSON response with duration and exit code, and CLI test command generator with copy functionality for terminal reproduction.
problem_statement: Users creating or editing hooks have no way to test them within the Blaze UI. They must manually construct JSON payloads, pipe them to hook scripts via terminal, and interpret raw output. This friction slows hook development and makes it difficult to verify hooks work correctly before enabling them in production sessions. We need an integrated test panel that lets users: (1) edit sample input JSON with syntax highlighting, (2) load predefined examples covering common scenarios, (3) execute the hook and see formatted output with timing, and (4) generate a CLI command to reproduce the test in terminal.

Hook scripts are executable and have correct permissions

FR4: Safe File button shall load example with file_path set to project-relative test.txt
FR5: Dangerous Path button shall load example with file_path set to /etc/passwd to test security hooks
FR6: Custom button shall load minimal template with all required HookInput fields
FR7: Run Test button shall spawn Process with hook command piping JSON input to stdin

FR10: Output panel shall display hook stdout formatted as indented JSON if parseable
FR11: Output panel shall display raw text if stdout is not valid JSON
FR12: Duration label shall show execution time in milliseconds with ms suffix
FR13: Exit code shall display with green checkmark for 0 or red X for non-zero
FR14: Copy Output button shall copy raw stdout content to system clipboard
FR15: Copy CLI Test button shall copy shell command reproducing the test

implementation_steps: Step 1: Create HookTestPanelView.swift file in Blaze/Sources/Settings/Hooks/ directory
Step 2: Define HookTestPanelView struct conforming to View with @Binding var hook: HookDefinition
Step 3: Add @State properties: inputJSON (String), outputText (String), isRunning (Bool), exitCode (Int?), durationMs (Int?)
Step 4: Add @State property jsonError (String?) for validation error display
Step 5: Define private struct TestExample with name (String) and json (String) properties
Step 6: Create static let examples array with Safe File, Dangerous Path, and Custom test cases
Step 7: Define Safe File example JSON with session_id, hook_event_name PreToolUse, tool_name Write, tool_input with safe file_path
Step 8: Define Dangerous Path example JSON with tool_input.file_path set to /etc/passwd
Step 9: Define Custom example JSON with placeholder values and comments for user editing
Step 10: Implement validateJSON() method returning Bool and setting jsonError state
Step 11: Build VStack layout with Section headers for Sample Input, Actions, and Output
Step 12: Implement input editor using TextEditor with .font(.system(.body, design: .monospaced))
Step 13: Add JSON validation badge overlay showing checkmark or error icon with tooltip
Step 14: Implement example loader HStack with three buttons styled with .buttonStyle(.bordered)
Step 15: Implement Run Test button with conditional ProgressView when isRunning is true
Step 16: Add .keyboardShortcut(.return, modifiers: .command) to Run Test button
Step 17: Implement runTest() async method using Process and Pipe for execution
Step 18: Configure Process with hook.command, set standardInput to Pipe with inputJSON data
Step 19: Capture stdout and stderr via Pipe.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile()
Step 20: Measure execution time using ContinuousClock.now before and after process.run()
Step 21: Calculate duration as elapsed.components.milliseconds and store in durationMs
Step 22: Parse stdout as JSON and pretty-print with JSONSerialization.WritingOptions.prettyPrinted
Step 23: Build output display Section with formatted output in scrollable Text view
Step 24: Display duration and exit code in HStack below output with appropriate icons
Step 25: Implement Copy Output button using NSPasteboard.general.setString()
Step 26: Implement generateCLICommand() returning properly escaped echo pipe bash command
Step 27: Implement Copy CLI Test button copying generated command to clipboard
Step 28: Add CLI command preview Text view with monospace font and selection enabled
Step 29: Add .accessibilityLabel modifiers to all buttons and status indicators
Step 30: Add .disabled(isRunning || jsonError != nil) modifier to Run Test button

edge_cases: Edge case 1: Hook script file does not exist - display File not found error with path in output area
Edge case 2: Hook script lacks execute permission - display Permission denied error in output area
Edge case 3: Hook produces no stdout - display No output from hook message in output area
Edge case 4: Hook produces invalid JSON in stdout - display raw text without formatting
Edge case 5: Hook produces very large output over 1MB - truncate with Output truncated warning
Edge case 6: Hook hangs and times out after 30 seconds - terminate process and show timeout message
Edge case 7: User navigates away during execution - cancel running process via task cancellation
Edge case 8: Input JSON contains special shell characters - properly escape in CLI command generation
Edge case 9: Hook writes to stderr instead of stdout - capture and display stderr content below stdout
Edge case 10: Hook command contains spaces in path - properly quote path in CLI command
Edge case 11: User rapidly clicks Run Test multiple times - debounce and prevent concurrent executions
Edge case 12: Input editor loses focus during JSON entry - preserve partial input without validation trigger
failure_modes: FM1: Process spawn fails due to missing executable - display error Could not execute hook: File not found
FM2: Process spawn fails due to permission denied - display error Could not execute hook: Permission denied
FM3: Hook crashes with signal - display Terminated by signal {signal} with exit code
FM4: Hook timeout after 30 seconds - display Timeout after 30 seconds, terminate process
FM5: Memory pressure during large output - truncate output and warn user
FM6: Clipboard write fails - show brief error toast Unable to copy to clipboard
FM7: JSON parsing fails for pretty-print - fall back to raw text display
FM8: Shell escaping fails for unusual characters - show warning that CLI command may need manual adjustment

risks: Risk 1: TextEditor may not provide adequate JSON editing experience without syntax highlighting
Risk 2: Process spawning may fail silently on sandboxed apps if entitlements missing
Risk 3: Large hook outputs could cause UI performance issues
Risk 4: Shell escaping edge cases could produce non-executable CLI commands
Risk 5: Hook execution could hang indefinitely if timeout mechanism fails
mitigations: Mitigation 1: Use monospace font and clear validation feedback to improve editing UX
Mitigation 2: Check entitlements and provide clear error message if process spawn fails
Mitigation 3: Truncate output over 1MB and warn user about partial display
Mitigation 4: Add integration test that executes generated CLI commands to verify escaping
Mitigation 5: Use Task timeout pattern with forced process termination as backup
risk_register.blast_radius: Limited to hook testing workflow. Failure does not affect hook execution during actual sessions. Users can fall back to manual terminal testing if panel has issues.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If test panel proves unreliable, hide behind feature flag and document manual terminal testing workflow as alternative. No data loss possible as panel has no persistent state.
